A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVM/MMCL research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v4 reports original numerical simulations, MPI3D-Complex and Causal3DIdent experiments, downstream evaluations, and ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds LAION-400M caption analysis and an OpenCLIP zero-shot evaluation on collected Flickr images.

M1.justification: The selection/perturbation-bias LVM, MMCL objectives, and existing encoder and training procedures remain unchanged. The OpenCLIP addition evaluates pretrained models without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds LAION-400M caption analysis and Flickr-based zero-shot concept recognition, organized around a stated 146-concept, 15-group taxonomy. This substantially extends coverage beyond numerical simulations and controlled 3D datasets to natural images and diverse concrete, abstract, and social concepts.

E2.justification: Existing linear and nonlinear probing comparisons are retained. OpenCLIP ViT-B-32 and ViT-L-14 are analyzed model configurations in the new case study; no competing algorithm is added against the proposed framework.

E3.justification: The new study introduces within-group zero-shot classification using concept-name prompts, pretrained ViT-B-32/ViT-L-14 models, and macro-F1, alongside caption coverage measured through concept and synonym matches. These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing experimental splits, budgets, and probing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The OpenCLIP case study examines the relationship between caption coverage and representation quality, with concept-level frequency analysis and within-group confusion matrices in Appendix G. These add substantial diagnostic evidence. Existing dimensionality ablations, joint-bias tests, linearity analyses, and OOD evaluations are retained.

E5.justification: Existing three-seed averaging and variability displays remain unchanged. The new study reports point estimates and descriptive distributions across concepts, without introducing repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v5 adds caption-coverage results, zero-shot scores, and confusion matrices. Figure 10 reports Animal macro-F1 of 97.6%/98.9% and Emot. of 19.5%/20.1% for ViT-B-32/ViT-L-14. These are newly reported evaluations; the retained simulation and 3D-dataset results match v4.

T1.justification: The assumptions, identifiability theorem, corollaries, and proofs retain their mathematical substance. Definition C.1 spells out the graded lexicographic ordering already specified and illustrated in v4's Clarification B.2; it does not introduce a different ordering or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same identifiability claims and application-dependent account of misalignment. The introduction adds mention of the pretrained-CLIP case study as supporting evidence, without changing the central scientific claims.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands interpretation through the OpenCLIP coverage/performance findings and distinctions between useful under-captioned concepts and sensitive concepts. Appendix I.1 adds substantive boundaries concerning bias estimation, other forms of misalignment, and emergent cross-modal semantics, while retaining the earlier missingness and linearity limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds collection and manual-filtering procedures, concept taxonomy, per-concept image counts, prompting details, and pretrained model names. The code-link repository spelling changes from mislaignment to misalignment. Existing implementation, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to Barsalou's Grounded Cognition, OpenCLIP, and Yarom et al.'s text-image alignment evaluation. The earlier references and substantive related-work positioning are retained; moving related work to Appendix B is organizational.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 6 to Appendix B, contributions become bullets, section titles are clarified, and discussion is reorganized into limitations and broader implications. Most existing prose remains unchanged, so the editorial revision is limited.

P2.justification: v5 adds coverage and F1 plots, detailed concept-frequency and confusion-matrix panels, and taxonomy/count tables (Figures 9–10 and 22–23; Tables 12–13). Existing heatmaps are recolored, bias labels clarified, and example-image displays resized or replaced, substantially extending and revising the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful applicability discussion and a natural-image case study while retaining v4's theory and controlled results. However, Table 13 lists 124 dog images whereas Figure 23's dog row totals 200; the stereotype classes also differ between Table 12 and Figure 23. These unresolved inconsistencies undermine the principal new validation, making the net quality effect uncertain.
